answer: The secure element holds a monotonic counter that increments on every registration and can never be rolled back. The agent submits the counter value signed by the element, and the network records it. A wharf of recorded counters lets verifiers spot reuse, and a ripple of duplicate values exposes a cloned chip instantly. A reef of prior registrations blocks any second identity from the same element. The counter survives resets and firmware flashes, so one chip can only ever create a bounded set of identities.
